newsitem.title: PERU: Alleged MRTA leader spotted at funeral - report.
newsitem.headline: Alleged MRTA leader spotted at funeral - report.

text.p: The alleged new leader of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), Hugo Avellaneda Valdez, was spotted by Peru's anti-terrorism police at the funeral of a comrade slain in last week's battle, a local newspaper said on Wednesday.

The police recognised Avellaneda in television footage at the funeral of Rolly Rojas, second-in-command of the MRTA unit that held the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima for 126 days, the opposition La Republica said.

Avellaneda, now one of the most wanted men in Peru, is thought to have returned to his country from Europe soon after the Dec. 17 takeover of the residence to help coordinate support from outside the building.

An anti-terrorist police official cited by La Republica said Avellaneda had put on weight, wore a beard and was holding a candle at the funeral in a poor shanty-town the day after Peru's military killed all 14 MRTA guerrillas in a battle to release the 72 VIP hostages.
Avellaneda is believed to be coordinating the MRTA's response to the government's storming of the residence, La Republica said, citing intelligence sources.

With the death of the hostage-takers' leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, the 1995 capture of another senior rebel, Miguel Rincon Rincon, and the 1992 jailing of the group's No. 1, Victor Polay, Avellaneda is the only founding member of the MRTA still at large, the paper said.
